subject: Provisioning degradation evidence and customer remediation schedule
messages:
From: Jane Miller <ops@acmeretail.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Provisioning degradation observed - us-west serving slowdowns

Hi Lauren / Ben,

We started seeing sustained latency increases and refused allocations against our dedicated pool in us-west starting ~07:50 PDT this morning. The pattern: token generation latency spikes from ~40ms to 400-700ms under similar QPS, and several requests were queued longer than 12s. Autoscaling did not appear to provision additional reserved nodes. Our incident tracker shows elevated 503s correlating with queue depth.

I attached a short capture (acme_latency_capture.log) with request IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood-side provisioning/allocator problem or something on our end? We need:
- Confirmation of root cause or immediate mitigation plan
- ETA for remediation and evidence package for our SRE and security teams
- Any interim workarounds (routing, model pinning, region shift) you recommend

This is impacting customer-facing checkout flows; we’d like a remediation ETA within 2 hours if possible. We’re willing to schedule a short phone bridge.

Thanks,
Jane Miller
Ops Lead, Acme Retail

Subject: Re: Provisioning degradation observed - us-west serving slowdowns

On Mon, Jul 31, 2028 at 8:12 AM Jane Miller <ops@acmeretail.com> wrote:
> We started seeing sustained latency increases ... Autoscaling did not appear to provision additional reserved nodes.

Thanks, Jane — I pulled the allocator and provisioning traces for your tenant. Short summary of findings so far (preliminary):

1) Allocator decision loop entered backoff at 07:48:12 PDT when a metadata lock delay coincided with a cloud API throttling window. The allocator retried but the backoff doubled; as a result, the autoscaler’s reserve-request call to the cloud provider was delayed by ~95s.
2) There was a transient mismatch between the model variant pinned by your routing policy (gptx-quant-v2) and the fallback group available on the warm-nodes pool; the runtime attempted a kernel-path that had a longer cold-start latency under our current quantization path.
3) We observed several concurrent cache misses in prefix/KV cache during that window which amplified per-request latency.

Immediate mitigation we will execute (planned start 09:20 PDT):
- Force-provision 2 reserved nodes into your dedicated pool (workaround)
- Temporarily route 20% of traffic to eu-west as a tested diversion path (if you approve)
- Apply a hotfix to allocator retry timing to avoid pathological backoff for cloud API throttle windows

Deliverables and timeline:
- 10:00 PDT: remediation started (force provisioning + traffic routing)
- 12:30 PDT: evidence bundle (allocator traces, provisioning events, kernel selection logs, KV-cache dump) uploaded to shared Drive
- 16:00 PDT: post-incident summary and proposed credit calculation

I’ll push an initial change to the routing config and kick off provisioning now. If Jane is okay with the eu-west diversion, please confirm so we can enable it at 09:25.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 02 Aug 2028 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Completed remediation, evidence bundle, and customer recovery schedule

Hi Jane (and Ravi),

Follow-up on the us-west provisioning degradation: the immediate remediation actions completed as planned and we validated reduced latency across your representative test group. Summary of what we delivered and next steps:

- What we changed:
  - Force-provisioned 2 reserved nodes into Acme Retail’s dedicated pool at 09:20 PDT on Jul 31 (cloud request IDs included in evidence bundle).
  - Temporarily diverted 20% of traffic to eu-west for a 3-hour window; that was reverted once pool capacity returned to steady state.
  - Applied allocator retry-timing hotfix (deployed 11:05 PDT) to prevent exponential backoff amplifying under cloud throttle conditions.
  - Tuned model fallback path to prefer warm-node compatible kernel variants for pinned model family.

- Evidence delivered: remediation-evidence.zip (allocator-traces.tar.gz, provisioning-events.log, kernel-selection.log, kv-cache-state.json) and allocation-timeline.csv summarizing event timestamps. Both are available here: https://drive.redwood.ai/file/d/1a2b3c-acme-evidence

- Impact and verification:
  - Peak 95th latency during the incident window returned to baseline within 25 minutes of force-provisioning.
  - No further queue-length anomalies observed after the allocation stabilized.

- Credits and next steps:
  - We will propose a credit equal to one week of Dedicated pool overage charges; Ben will circulate the calculation by Friday.
  - We recommend a short architecture review with your SREs to discuss fallback policies, KV-cache warming, and optional proactive warm-node commitments. I’ll coordinate a 30-minute session next week if that suits you.

If you need additional artifacts (signed timeline, notarized log extracts for audits), we can provide those. Thanks again for the prompt signals which helped us diagnose faster.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
